Maria Chen: FYI ran into a weird one while onboarding hf/model-x -> Redwood. After merging added_tokens.json the BOS/EOS ids appear shifted and chat templates break (responses truncated or body prepended with "<|unk|>").
Alex Rivera: can you paste the tokenizer_config/config.json and a small snippet of added_tokens.json?
Maria Chen: sure — minimal repro below. I converted with the usual hf->redwood tool then quantized. Observed mismatch only after quantizing with 4-bit qat.
Maria Chen: ```
// added_tokens.json (excerpt)
[{"content":"<|special_emoji|>", "id":50256}, {"content":"<|custom_bos|>", "id":50257}]
// tokenizer_config.json (excerpt)
{"bos_token": "<|custom_bos|>", "eos_token": "<|endoftext|>", "unk_token": "<|unk|>"}
```
Jordan Patel: hmmm. If added_tokens were appended during conversion but the tokenizer model (sentencepiece/bpe) reindexed because quantized weights changed export ordering, the numeric ids in added_tokens.json won't line up with the tokenizer's internal vocab. Try running `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(["<|custom_bos|>"])` against the converted tokenizer file and see what it returns.
Maria Chen: ran that. HF tokenizer says id 50257 but Redwood runtime resolves BOS->50258. So off by +1 in runtime mapping.
Ben Liu: did you check special_tokens_map / tokenizers.json? sometimes the conversion script writes both added_tokens.json and a separate mapping and they disagree. Also check if `pad_token` was newly inserted — insertion shifts indices.
Maria Chen: good catch. pad_token was auto-inserted during quant export. I didn't notice.
Alex Rivera: workaround: remap on load with patch to the conversion script. Pseudocode: `for t in added_tokens: actual_id = tokenizer.token_to_id(t['content']); if actual_id != t['id']: remap_table[t['id']] = actual_id` then write a small `special_token_remap.json` consumed by Redwood loader.
Jordan Patel: or better: when you quantize, freeze tokenizer ordering by exporting the final tokenizer model (tokenizer.json / merges / vocab) and regenerate added_tokens with correct ids: `reindexed = [{"content":t, "id":tokenizer.token_to_id(t)} for t in original_added]`. That avoids runtime patches.
Maria Chen: posted repro script in gist: https://internal.gist/repro-1965432100 (private). Repro steps: 1) hf load 2) attach added_tokens.json 3) export 4-bit quant -> observe tests/chatbot fails.
Ben Liu: did evals catch it? It caused ~6% drop on our conv. quality metric and some formatting regressions on the chat template tests. Put a hold on that model pipeline in CI until patched.
hug_sync_bot: huggingface sync: uploaded model-x-quant4 -> destination: s3://redwood-models/staging/model-x-quant4 (checksum OK)
Alex Rivera: quick sed-based patch if you need to unblock: `jq '.[] |= if .id==50256 then .id=TOKENIZER_ID_50256 else . end' added_tokens.json` after computing `TOKENIZER_ID_50256` from tokenizer. Not ideal long term.
Maria Chen: I'll regenerate added_tokens from the exported tokenizer and push a conversion patch. Scheduling a small migration job to reindex the staging models.
Jordan Patel: also add a post-conversion check in the importer: assert all added_tokens ids == tokenizer.token_to_id(content) and fail early.
Maria Chen: agreed. I'll open a PR with repro + fix + a unit test. ETA EOD tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
